Timeline::quarter¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::quarter() const

quarter() is the sole public spelling.

Group Months Into Calendar Quarters¶

quarter() returns 1, 2, 3, or 4 according to the local calendar month: January-March, April-June, July-September, and October-December. The method uses ordinary calendar quarters beginning in January; it does not infer an organization’s fiscal-year offset.

The result is an int32 Series with exactly the Timeline’s shape. NaT maps to -1.

Example: Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto schedule = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-04-01T00:00:00Z"},
    {"2024-07-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-10-01T00:00:00Z"},
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, schedule.quarter());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1 2 ⎤
⎣ 3 4 ⎦

This demonstrates that extraction is not limited to timestamp columns. Every position in a multidimensional Timeline is projected independently.

Calendar Versus Fiscal Quarters¶

For a calendar year, the returned value can be used directly with year() as a (year, quarter) grouping key. If a fiscal year starts in another month, first define that business rule explicitly; merely relabeling Q1 would leave the associated year boundary ambiguous.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Quarter numbering is one-based.

  • The method has no fiscal-year-start argument.

  • A quarter number alone is not unique; retain the corresponding year.

  • -1 denotes NaT and is outside the valid range.
